correctness.rationale: From nonnegative GBC plus affine precision, numerator for every vertex off a facet vanishes on that facet; if a facet form divided reduced q then normalized and weighted sums force it to divide every numerator, contradiction. At nonadjacent support-line intersections all numerators and hence q vanish. Each side has at most one parallel opposite side, and distinct nonadjacent nonparallel support-line intersections are distinct; restriction q|side has ≥m−4 roots (m−3 without parallel mate). Wachspress adjoint side restriction is a constant times the product of those nonadjacent side forms. In all-paired case any reduced q of degree≤m−4 restricts proportionally to adjoint on every side; vertex values propagate common factor and m side factors force polynomial equality, excluding lower degree or a nongeneric different adjoint. The cited Baumbach et al. Cor4.6 yields deg adjoint m−4 precisely for central symmetry and m−3 otherwise. Independent SymPy exact affine precision, side restrictions and degrees for triangle/parallelogram/trapezoid/pentagon; these examples are diagnostics, analytic facet/root argument proves all m.

final_claim: For each convex m-gon, the minimum degree of a common polynomial denominator for nonnegative rational generalized barycentric coordinates equals Wachspress adjoint degree: m−4 for centrally symmetric polygons and m−3 otherwise; in the low-degree case every reduced denominator is proportional to the adjoint.
limitations: Requires convex polygon, nonnegative continuous rational generalized barycentric coordinates and a common polynomial denominator.
The cited adjoint-degree classification is prior material and not asserted original.
